Write this in my voice (email, external): the deliverable is late by a week because the vendor missed the API deadline; offer a call Thursday.
expected_behavior: runs pick_exemplars.py for email-external, reads the length budget and skeleton, and drafts within the budget copying the skeleton's greeting/sign-off classes
uses only the facts in the brief and marks anything unknown (e.g. the recipient's name, Thursday time) with [?]
runs voice_check.py on the draft with --brief and --exemplars, reports the verdict, and fixes FAILs before presenting
never sends or posts anything; presents the draft for the user to edit
does not inflate: no opener the profile never uses, no extra pleasantries, no closing recap

cases.prompt: Reply to this as me: <pasted 3-line email from a partner asking for the numbers by Friday>. Answer: rough cut Friday, final next week.
expected_behavior: uses --reply-to so the reply length tracks the incoming message and picks reply exemplars
answers in sentence one, keeps the register's usual greeting/sign-off distribution rather than defaulting to formal

cases.prompt: Write my resignation email in my voice.
expected_behavior: says this is a high-stakes message, keeps the draft minimal, and recommends the user writes the first and last line themselves
still drafts if the user confirms, with [?] for dates and names

cases.prompt: make this sound like me (no profile exists yet)
expected_behavior: explains that voice-corpus and voice-profile must run first and offers to do so; if the user wants a draft anyway, labels it as not in their voice

cases.prompt: Write it in my voice but I don't want you to read my samples into context this time.
expected_behavior: uses --minimal (profile constraints only, no exemplars) and says the draft will match structure and bans but less of the rhythm
